title: Untitled

for: The method divides return history into segments with different mean and variance, and change points indicate where a Gaussian with its own mean/variance on each side fits better than a single Gaussian by more than the penalty
Segmentation is applied to logarithmic returns (not raw prices), which strip out price level and isolate shifts in return distribution

The cost function C(s, e) = n * ln(max(var, ε)) is explicitly defined and used to score segment fit; it is the -2 ln L of a Gaussian likelihood (with constants dropped), making it testable as a model-based objective
The automatic penalty β = 2·ln(n) is applied when InpPenalty is zero/negative — a BIC-style penalty corresponding to two parameters (mean and variance) per segment

Sensitivity scan varies penalty (×0.5, ×1, ×2, ×3), minimum segment length (5, 10, 20), and lookback (0.8×, 1.0×, 1.2×) and reports which change points persist across settings — e.g., 'January and April 2026 boundaries [...] are preserved at minimum lengths 10 and 20 and at all three lookbacks'

Output includes mean and volatility of each segment before/after each change point — e.g., Segment 2 shows volatility ~1.8× higher than next-highest segment, bracketed by two change points only 16 returns apart
The script computes exact optimal segmentation (via PELT) for the floored Gaussian objective, and the result is fully reproducible given same data and settings

against: The method is retrospective. It marks up history and is not a trading signal. Because each segment must be at least a minimum length, it cannot report a change point in the last few bars, and change points near the end of the window can shift when new data arrives.

It is not a hypothesis test. 'Statistical' here means derived from a Gaussian mean-and-variance segmentation model with a given penalty. There is no p-value or confidence level behind any individual break.

Repeatable does not mean assumption-free. The same data and settings always give the same answer, but the cost function, the penalty and the minimum segment length are choices, and different choices give different segmentations.

The output is a dated segmentation of a return history, useful as a basis for regime-conditioned testing of a strategy, for studying whether position-sizing rules should depend on volatility regimes, or simply as a record of when the modeled volatility of an instrument changed.
The class can also be used from an Expert Advisor, but that does not turn its output into a validated real-time signal. It only means the same retrospective analysis can be re-run periodically.
non_fatal: Spread and commissions are not considered.
No live forward test is presented.
No discussion of latency or execution feasibility for real-time use.

judge.reject_reason: Статья описывает метод обнаружения точек структурных разрывов (change point detection) в исторических логарифмических доходностях, но НЕ формулирует торговое правило для входа в сделку. В тексте чётко указано, что метод 'retrospective', 'is not a trading signal', 'cannot report a change point in the last few bars', и 'does not turn its output into a validated real-time signal'. Нет описания условия входа (направления, тайминга, параметров), нет указаний, как на основе обнаруженной точки разрыва открыть long/short позицию. Это инструмент анализа режимов, а не торговая стратегия. Отсутствие правила входа — фатальный порок по критериям.
judge.summary: Статья представляет реализацию алгоритма PELT для детектирования точек структурных разрывов в логарифмических доходностях с помощью гауссовой сегментации и штрафа за количество разрывов. Метод предназначен исключительно для ретроспективного анализа исторических данных и не является торговой системой.
